q: What is the CBAM default value for steel pipes and tubes from India?
title: CBAM default value: Indian steel pipes
short: Most Indian carbon steel pipes and tubes under CN 7304, 7305 and 7306 carry 4.320 t CO2e per tonne. Stainless line pipe, casing and tubing carry 6.490 or 6.500. Cast iron pipes under CN 7303 carry 2.840. Direct emissions only, plus the 2026 mark-up of 10%.
audience: Indian pipe and tube exporters, welded and non-welded, and their EU importers

sections.h: India default values, t CO2e per tonne
ul: CN 7303 cast iron tubes and pipes: 2.840
CN 7305 large welded pipes over 406.4 mm: 4.320
CN 7306 welded, carbon steel (such as 7306 30 and 7306 61 92): 4.320

p: The listed values are increased by a mark-up: 10% for 2026, 20% for 2027 and 30% from 2028. Goods imported in 2026 always take the 2026 mark-up.

A welded pipe mill buying HR coil can use the coil maker's verified figure as its precursor value instead of a default, then add its own forming and welding energy. Ask for the coil figure in the purchase contract.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so an actual figure you send an EU buyer can be traced back to the documents behind it. It does not file CBAM declarations.

sources.label: European Commission, Default values definitive period (Excel, version 2 of 6 August 2026), India sheet; legally binding values in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1740 correcting (EU) 2025/2621
